sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Controlling Text Search
sources.version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; page reports 18 as current stable and 19 as development/beta at access
sources.locator: §12.3.1 document/query parsing; §12.3.3 ranking; tsvector, setweight, ts_rank, ts_rank_cd; lines 18-48 and 160-181
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL via browser tooling; read page text and section locators
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Text vectors use selected/default text-search configuration; dictionaries normalize/stem or discard stop words; title/body weights are caller-assigned; ranking docs describe relevance as application-specific; default rank weights are {0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0}.
sources.applicability: Primary lexical alternative; explains exact token and ranking behavior. Not semantic search, access control, or a calibrated authority/confidence score.
sources.evidence_summary: Postgres FTS parses to tsvector and ranks using lexical, proximity, and structural signals; rank is application-specific.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: GIN Indexes
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL and followed find for full-text search
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: GIN supports inverted lookup including document lexemes; gin_fuzzy_search_limit defaults to 0 (no limit); nonzero returns a soft, random subset, not a top-ranked truncation.
sources.applicability: Supports lexical FTS and an important completeness caveat if the non-default fuzzy limit is enabled.
sources.evidence_summary: GIN is an inverted index for composite values such as documents; a nonzero soft limit is not deterministic ranking.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Row Security Policies
sources.locator: §5.9 opening behavior, owner/superuser bypass, policy composition
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL and read policy conditions
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RLS must be enabled; with no policies behavior is default-deny. Table owners normally bypass; superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass. Multiple permissive policies combine with OR; restrictive policies with AND. TRUNCATE and REFERENCES are outside RLS.
sources.applicability: Authorization alternative if content and search rows are in PostgreSQL; app connections must not run as privileged owner/bypass roles and all read paths need review.
sources.evidence_summary: RLS is a row-query boundary with explicit privilege and command exceptions, not a generic cache or citation policy.

sources.title: pgvector README at v0.8.7
sources.version_or_commit: Release v0.8.7, tag commit shown as f37c13f
sources.locator: Filtering; Multitenancy; Iterative Index Scans; HNSW/IVFFlat scan caps; lines 507-606
sources.observed_operation: Opened tag-pinned README and read filtered-search section
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Approximate-index filters are applied after initial scan; HNSW ef_search defaults to 40; iterative scans are optional since v0.8.0 and stop at scan/probe caps; strict/relaxed ordering differ; partition/separate table recommended for tenant isolation.
sources.applicability: PostgreSQL semantic-search option; ACL/selectivity can cause underfill and cross-tenant recall/performance effects. Version-pinned behavior must be rechecked against deployment.
sources.evidence_summary: pgvector exposes HNSW/IVFFlat trade-offs and explicitly documents filtered approximate recall limits.

sources.title: pgvector CHANGELOG at v0.8.7 and release
sources.version_or_commit: Release v0.8.7, tag commit f37c13f; release dated 2026-10-01
sources.observed_operation: Opened tag-pinned changelog; release page separately showed tag and short commit
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 0.8.7 fixes IVFFlat build buffer overflow; 0.8.3/0.8.4 include HNSW vacuum corruption/repair and insert fixes; 0.8.0 adds iterative scans and improves filtering cost estimation.
sources.applicability: Index build/vacuum lifecycle risk and version history; these changes do not establish query correctness for this corpus.
sources.evidence_summary: Maintained project history includes filtering improvements and later HNSW/IVFFlat lifecycle fixes.

sources.title: pgvector issue #719: SELECT WHERE ORDER BY LIMIT no results
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2024-11-26; reporter says pgvector 0.7.0; maintainer response points to 0.8.0
sources.locator: Description, query plans and maintainer comment recommending upgrade/B-tree for selective filter; lines 165-223
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue page and read reporter version, reproduction, and maintainer reply
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported result depended on selective relational filters over nearest-neighbor candidates; maintainer suggested v0.8.0 iterative filtering and B-tree for highly selective filters.
sources.applicability: Historical filtered HNSW failure showing no-result behavior can be a recall/filter-plan issue; does not prove all versions/cases fail.
sources.evidence_summary: A 0.7.0 report documented a filtered ANN query returning no rows; maintainer response suggested 0.8.0 and B-tree.

sources.title: pgvector issue #785: Continued filtered HNSW underfill and latency
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2025-02-25; reporter says pgvector 0.8.0, PostgreSQL 15; closed 2025-03-03
sources.locator: Reproduction/results and final activity; lines 145-221 and 227-246
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue; read reproduction, environment, and closure activity
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter describes zero/underfilled 100-neighbor results under restrictive filters and latency increasing with scan settings. Maintainer asked for query plan/cardinality, suggested B-tree and HNSW parameter review; issue closure did not document a code fix.
sources.applicability: Caution that iterative scans/caps and settings do not promise complete top-k under every filter. The issue is a report, not a general benchmark or verified regression.
sources.evidence_summary: An issue report and closure comment preserve a filtered underfill/latency case without a documented patch resolution.

sources.title: OpenSearch 3.8: Reciprocal rank fusion
sources.version_or_commit: OpenSearch documentation version 3.8; page banner says this version is no longer maintained; RRF introduced 2.19, normalization 2.10
sources.locator: Intro, combination-method comparison, example, default rank constant, and interpreting RRF scores
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned docs; read RRF formula, hybrid example, defaults/cautions
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RRF ranks by result positions and ignores raw score margin; default rank_constant is 60; docs advise against min_score thresholds and comparing RRF scores across queries. Normalization is score-based and preserves margins.
sources.applicability: Hybrid retrieval alternative; reasonable uncalibrated starting fusion, but requires synthetic/real relevance evaluation and a supported release check.
sources.evidence_summary: RRF fuses lexical and vector rank lists without equating raw score scales and has score-interpretation caveats.

sources.title: OpenSearch 3.8: Document-level security
sources.version_or_commit: OpenSearch documentation version 3.8; page banner says no longer maintained
sources.locator: DLS scope, identifier analyzer caveat, adaptive mode, multiple roles, write permissions
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned docs and read surrounding DLS/default/role sections
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: DLS constrains read retrieval, not writes; evaluation defaults to adaptive; DLS predicates across roles use OR with a documented override setting; text analyzers can split punctuation-bearing user IDs, so exact keyword/custom analyzer is needed.
sources.applicability: OpenSearch security mechanism to prototype; ACL field mapping, group combination, role configuration, version support, and revocation propagation require explicit testing.
sources.evidence_summary: DLS has behavior and mapping conditions that matter to authorization correctness; it is not sufficient proof of end-to-end revocation.

sources.title: OpenSearch 3.8: Filtering vector search results
sources.version_or_commit: OpenSearch documentation version 3.8; page banner says no longer maintained
sources.locator: Efficient k-NN filter, post-filter, scoring-script filter, engine/version support and recall/latency examples
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned docs and read filtering modes and support table
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Efficient filtering occurs in search for supported Lucene/Faiss methods; post-filter can return fewer than k; exact prefilter+scoring can be high latency for large candidate subsets; engine/method and version define support.
sources.applicability: Semantic retrieval alternative with access filters; evaluate selectivity, engine, recall and latency on the synthetic corpus.
sources.evidence_summary: Filter placement changes approximate recall and exact search cost.

sources.title: OpenSearch 3.8: k-NN methods and engines
sources.version_or_commit: OpenSearch documentation version 3.8; page banner says no longer maintained
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned docs; read engine comparison and recommendations
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: HNSW and IVF are supported methods; engines have differing capabilities. Docs recommend Faiss for large scale, Lucene for smaller deployment/smart filtering, JVector for high updates/memory-constrained cases; version, extension, hardware and workload conditions apply.
sources.applicability: Alternatives within OpenSearch; recommendations are vendor guidance, not workload-independent findings.
sources.evidence_summary: The OpenSearch vector choice is a method/engine trade-off rather than a single undifferentiated k-NN feature.

sources.title: OpenSearch 3.8: Index aliases
sources.version_or_commit: OpenSearch documentation version 3.8; page banner says no longer maintained
sources.locator: Switching an alias to a different index and alias characteristics
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned docs and read reindex/cutover behavior
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: An alias can switch to a fully built index without downtime by combined remove/add; change is atomic. Multi-index writes need a designated write index; later wildcard-created indexes are not automatically added.
sources.applicability: Can support index-generation cutover, but does not supply ingestion state, authority versioning, or authorization freshness.
sources.evidence_summary: Aliases provide a concrete atomic active-generation switch after reindex.

sources.title: W3C Web Annotation Data Model
sources.locator: TextQuoteSelector §4.2.4; TextPositionSelector §4.2.5; canonical identity §3.3.7; representation state
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C specification and read selector definitions and caveats
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Quote selector carries normalized selected text with context; position selector is representation-relative and spec warns it is brittle under edits/transclusion, recommending a state to identify the representation.
sources.applicability: Locator design vocabulary, not a version store, authorization mechanism, or promise of immutability.
sources.evidence_summary: Quote-plus-context and offsets are alternative passage selectors; offsets need representation state.

sources.title: Elasticsearch document/field-level security limitations
sources.version_or_commit: Current Elasticsearch documentation as accessed 2026-10-12; release version not stated in page
sources.locator: DLS limitations; aggregate-information note; request-cache exception
sources.observed_operation: Opened current vendor docs and used find on aggregate/cache limitations
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Vendor states DLS can leave aggregate information over restricted records observable; request cache is disabled for specified templated-stored-script and mixed local/remote index conditions, not universally.
sources.applicability: Counterexample to assuming per-document filtering alone protects counts/terms; Elastic-specific statement, must not be generalized to OpenSearch/PostgreSQL.
sources.evidence_summary: Search security can still expose aggregate facts, and cache exceptions are conditional.

sources.title: Elasticsearch node query cache settings
sources.version_or_commit: Current Elasticsearch Reference as accessed 2026-10-12; release version not stated in page
sources.observed_operation: Opened current vendor reference; read cache scope and defaults
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filter-context query results are cached per segment in a node query cache shared by shards; default index setting enables query caching, maximum 10,000 queries/up to 10% heap; segment merges invalidate segment caches.
sources.applicability: Shows a cache layer exists in one candidate family; does not describe application/browser cache security. Require chosen system’s cache identity and ACL-revocation tests.
sources.evidence_summary: Engine cache scope and invalidation differ from app-level result/snippet caches.
